hints: Write the equation of the normal and solve for its $x$-intercept ($y = 0$).
walkthrough:
Differentiate the curve equation with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2} - \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)(x - 2)^{-4/3} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3(x - 2)^{4/3}}$$

Evaluate the gradient of the tangent at $A\left(3, \frac{6}{5}\right)$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=3} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3(3 - 2)^{4/3}} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{5}{6}$$

Determine the gradient of the normal line perpendicular to the tangent:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{5/6} = -\frac{6}{5}$$

Form the equation of the normal passing through $A\left(3, \frac{6}{5}\right)$:
$$y - \frac{6}{5} = -\frac{6}{5}(x - 3)$$

Set $y = 0$ to find the $x$-intercept:
$$0 - \frac{6}{5} = -\frac{6}{5}(x - 3) \implies x - 3 = 1 \implies x = 4$$

ai_rubric.Tangents and Normals: Differentiates to $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3(x - 2)^{4/3}}$ (B1). Finds gradient $5/6$ at $x=3$ (M1). Finds normal gradient $-6/5$ (DM1). Sets up normal line (DM1). Obtains $x = 4$ (A1).

skill_tags: Finding an Area Under a Curve

hints: Calculate the triangular area under the normal from $x = 3$ to $x = 4$: $\frac{1}{2}(1)\left(\frac{6}{5}\right) = 0.6$.
Sum both areas and round to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Set up and evaluate the definite integral for the area under the curve from $x = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5$ to $x = 3$:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{curve}} = \int_{2.5}^3 \left(\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{7}{10} - (x - 2)^{-1/3}\right) dx = \left[ \frac{1}{4}x^2 + \frac{7}{10}x - \frac{3}{2}(x - 2)^{2/3} \right]_{2.5}^3$$

Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle under the normal from $x = 3$ to the intercept at $x = 4$:
$$\text{Area}_{\triangle} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times (4 - 3) \times \frac{6}{5} = \frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 1.2 = 0.6$$

Sum both areas to obtain the total shaded area:
$$\text{Total Area} = 0.48244 + 0.6 = 1.08244 \approx 1.08 \quad (\text{to 2 d.p.})$$

ai_rubric.Definite Integration: Integrates curve to $\frac{1}{4}x^2 + \frac{7}{10}x - \frac{3}{2}(x - 2)^{2/3}$ (M1, A1). Substitutes limits $2.5$ and $3$ (M1) to get $0.4824$ (A1). Adds triangle area $0.6$ (B1). Obtains total area $1.08$ (A1).
